content.title: About
content.content: Clams are marine bivalve mollusks that are often prepared fried. Fried clams have tender meat, a slightly sweet flavor, and a crisp crust. They are commonly served as an appetizer or as a component of Asian and Mediterranean dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Clams filter water, helping to clean it of microscopic particles.
In the wild clams can live up to 20 years, but culinary use usually involves younger specimens.
Frying clams is often done with oil, garlic, ginger, or spices to enhance aroma.
Clams are rich in iron and vitamin B12, making them valuable for pescatarians.
In some countries clams are considered a delicacy and are served in high‑end restaurants.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Clams provide complete protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Iron source
items.content: The iron in clams is highly bioavailable and supports hemoglobin levels.

items.title: Vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is essential for nervous system function and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Clams contain EPA and DHA, which promote heart and vascular health.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Clams supply zinc, selenium and magnesium, contributing to immunity and metabolism.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to clams, ranging from skin rash to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Toxin contamination
items.content: Clams can accumulate toxins and heavy metals from polluted waters; purchase from reputable sources.

items.title: Food poisoning
items.content: Undercooked clams may harbor pathogenic bacteria that cause gastroenteritis.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: When served with soy sauce or added salt, clams can become a source of excess sodium.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fried clams are served hot, often with a dipping sauce made from soy sauce, lemon juice, or spicy chili. They can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, added to salads, noodles, or rice dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh clams in the refrigerator in a sealed container for no more than 1‑2 days. Fried clams are best consumed within 24 hours; if needed, store them in an airtight container in the fridge.
